messages:
emma_cs: Heads-up — Pinwheel seeing consistent 429s during SDK bootstrap in eu-west when a new release does a mass reconnect. Happening within first 30s of rollout.

emma_cs: Minimal log from their edge: ```POST /v1/sdk/init  HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
x-request-id: pin-req-83b
x-region: eu-west-1
Response: 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 14
```

emma_cs: They say the surge is ~600 clients within 20s, each opening a short-lived socket and doing an ephemeral token exchange. Any quick mitigation we can recommend?

raj_eng: Can they attach the client-side config? curious about keepAlive, token rotation frequency, and any parallel preflight calls. Also need request ids for a couple of failures (we can trace).

pinwheel-dev: attaching a trimmed config, they use our browser SDK default bootstrapper. They rotate ephemeral tokens every 10s (we thought that was fine). SDK init call stack: ```await Redwood.init({ envKey: 'pk_live_xxx', ephemeralTTL: 10, enablePrefetch: true })```

pinwheel-dev: sample headers for one fail: ```x-request-id: pin-req-83b
x-client-conns: 614
x-forwarded-for: 18.205.3.12
```

leo_dev: Two obvious things to recommend now: 1) increase ephemeralTTL to 120s so they don't hammer auth, 2) enable connection reuse/keepAlive on their clients (browser service worker or edge proxy) so requests are multiplexed instead of N * new TCP. Example quick patch: ```// client shim
Redwood.init({ ephemeralTTL: 120, maxParallelInits: 6, enablePrefetch: true })```

leo_dev: Also we should add a server-side short-term backpressure header to hint clients to back off — but that's infra work.

kai_infra: On infra side I see a pattern where a burst of ephemeral token validation + new sessions triggers our route to Dedicated auth pool and it saturates auth QPS briefly. Short-term workaround: enable auth token batching on our edge (we can coalesce identical token validation calls for 5s). I'll spin a tiny feature flag.

kai_infra: Can we coordinate a live test window? I'll enable batching for their account id for 10 minutes and watch. Tagging @onboard-bot to open a temporary flag request.

onboard-bot: Ticket created: CS-#4321 — "Pinwheel bootstrap 429 spike". Assigned to raj_eng, kai_infra. ETA for flag rollout: ~15m.

onboard-bot: Added playbook link: https://confluence.redwood/integration-playbooks/bootstrap-backpressure (internal) :white_check_mark:

emma_cs: Thanks — I'll tell Pinwheel to flip ephemeralTTL to 120 and add a brief stagger on release (5s splay). Also to report any x-request-id values if they still see 429s.

pinwheel-dev: Doing TTL change now on canary. Will roll 10% -> 100% over 2 mins and report back. Thx! :pray:

raj_eng: If 429s persist after TTL increase, collect a pair of request ids and a short dump of their client connection counts. We can then correlate to our auth queue metrics and widen the mitigation.

leo_dev: Long-term ask for product: expose a client-side SDK option `splayOnInit` (small jitter window) and `prefetchConcurrency` controls in the browser SDK. That would reduce stampedes without docs gymnastics. I'll file a feature request.

emma_cs: Great. Logging this thread into the customer health record. Closing once Pinwheel confirms green. :thumbsup:
